questions.question: What service does TCP expose to an application?
options: A reliable, ordered byte stream with flow and congestion control
A guarantee that a remote transaction committed
questions.explanation: TCP preserves byte order and delivery while connected; applications still define messages and business outcomes.

questions.question: Why must an application frame messages on TCP?
options: One send does not correspond to one receive; bytes may be split or coalesced arbitrarily
questions.explanation: The socket exposes a stream, so the application needs a length, delimiter, or self-describing format.

questions.question: When can UDP be a strong fit for position updates?
options: When newer sequenced state supersedes stale updates and the application handles loss, order, pacing, and congestion
When every historical packet must arrive
When no packet can be authenticated
When the path MTU is unknown and datagrams are unbounded
questions.explanation: Latest-state semantics can prefer timely new data over transport retransmission of stale data.

questions.question: What is bandwidth-delay product?
options: The amount of data that can be in flight while filling a path at a given bandwidth and RTT
questions.explanation: A sender needs enough in-flight data and buffers to use a high-bandwidth, high-latency path.

questions.question: Why should UDP applications keep datagrams below the effective path MTU?
options: Fragmentation increases loss blast radius and is frequently filtered or handled inconsistently
UDP headers grow after every hop
questions.explanation: One lost fragment loses the whole datagram, and middleboxes make fragmented traffic fragile.

questions.question: Does TCP eliminate duplicate business side effects?
options: No; application retries and ambiguous failures still require idempotency and reconciliation
questions.explanation: Transport delivery is not the same as exactly-once execution of an external business operation.

questions.question: What happens when one TCP segment is missing?
options: Later stream bytes normally wait for recovery of the missing sequence, creating head-of-line delay
The application receives later bytes out of order
questions.explanation: TCP presents an ordered stream, so gaps must be recovered before later bytes are delivered in order.

questions.question: What responsibility remains when an application builds a protocol over UDP?
options: Congestion-safe pacing plus any required sequence, retry, expiry, deduplication, and security behavior
None, because UDP is always faster
questions.explanation: Removing TCP does not remove network or correctness responsibilities; it moves them upward.
